content:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — grafana shows a sharp SLO burn spike for gpu-serve-saturation in eu-west this morning. looks correlated with network flaps, many inflight reqs retried/evicted. screenshot in ops-runbook.

Jordan Lee: Can you paste the panel/query? which SLO are we measuring? :eyes:

Maya Patel: It's the "gpu-serve-saturation" composite SLO (uptime+saturation). current prom query for error rate:

```
sum by(region) (increase(requests_errors_total{handler="gpu-serve",job="proxy"}[5m]))
/ sum by(region) (increase(requests_total{handler="gpu-serve"}[5m]))
```

Maya Patel: Grafana shows eu-west at ~7% burn in last 5m, spike starts ~07:05, then back to baseline. logs show lots of `connection reset by peer` and `kubelet evicting pod` around same time.

Elena R: Two quick thoughts: 1) That query double-counts retries if the client re-issues requests — we'll overestimate error SLI during transient net blips. 2) Prometheus scrape gaps + histogram sparsity mean a single 5m window can look worse than reality.

Samir: Agree. We should define the SLI to be "successful end-to-end response within N retries" instead of raw request success. Practically we can: mark a request successful if either the proxy returns 2xx or the downstream indicates success in the trace/span.

Samir: Example approach (rough) — count successful unique request_ids from logs (not raw proxied http counts). But logs are heavy.

David K: Also watch scrape intervals. eu-west exporters had 15s jitter and a few missed scrapes 07:03-07:06. For alerting we should smooth burn rate: rolling_average(increase(...[30m])) to avoid one-window alerts.

oncall-bot: ALERT SLO_BURN_HIGH gpu-serve-saturation eu-west fired for rota=oncall (rule=slo:burn_rate:5m > 0.05)

Maya Patel: Proposed immediate changes:
- adjust alert rule: use 30m smoothed burn with a 1h evaluation window before paging
- add a panel "net-new errors (deduped by request_id)" that surfaces logs-sampled success vs errors
- add runbook step: if burn spike + kube evictions -> check node network/MTU flaps and evictions timeline

Jordan Lee: :+1: I'll open a PR for the alert rule and dashboard changes. Can we add a short TTL annotation to the SLO (temporary ignore) for known infra incidents to avoid noisy pages? maybe a suppression window when node-level outage is detected.

Elena R: We should also revisit SLI definition doc. current SLI is request success rate at proxy only. Propose changing to "per-tenant successful end-to-end within 2 retries" and exposing both proxy-level and end-to-end SLI on console.

Samir: For implementation: we can add a small sampling pipeline that tags logs with request_id and outcome, export to bigtable -> pre-aggregate per-minute counts. Low QPS tenants can be handled by sampling to avoid cost.

David K: Action owners:
- Jordan: PR to change alert smoothing + suppression rule (ETA: today EOD)
- Maya: update runbook with net-flap troubleshooting steps and attach sample logs (ETA: tomorrow)
- Elena: draft SLI change proposal and rollout plan (ETA: next Wed)
- Samir: prototype sampling pipeline (ETA: 2 weeks)

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. I'll mute the 5m alert paging for eu-west while we get the smoothing PR merged. :thumbsup:

Jordan Lee: filing the PR now: https://git.redwood.dev/infra/alerts/pulls/321

oncall-bot: NOTE: SLO_BURN_HIGH resolved for eu-west at 07:22

Maya Patel: keeping this thread for follow-ups. tagging @dave (network infra) to check MTU/eni logs if infra saw anything at 07:03-07:08

David K: noted, will loop in network team.
